slice.hypothesis: Google Calendar's connector-internal ETag-protected private-label write may expose enough caller-visible label/readback state to act as a deterministic finite-state compare-and-set coordination cell.
slice.tested_surface: list_event_labels, set_event_label_silently, read_event/batch_read_event contracts; generic update_event was not re-audited substantively beyond the inherited r245 comparison.
slice.tested_scope: Current Chat-exposed tool schema only. No calendars, events, labels, attendees, or other user semantic data were read or mutated.

evidence.label_catalog_contract: list_event_labels can resolve an existing label's exact name and UUID, but it exposes label identity rather than an event-local version/precondition token.
evidence.guarded_write_contract: set_event_label_silently accepts only event_id and label_id. The connector states that missing ETags fail before write and concurrent updates are protected with the current ETag; the caller cannot supply an expected ETag, expected prior label, version, idempotency key, or compare predicate.
evidence.event_read_contract: read_event/batch_read_event read full event details by ID, but their input contracts expose no version-bound read token that can be supplied back to set_event_label_silently. Even if the returned event detail includes the current private label, the exposed write has no caller-controlled precondition tying a subsequent mutation to that observed state.
evidence.atomicity_consequence: The schema supports a narrow lost-update-resistant blind assignment using the connector's internally current ETag, but not compare(observed state/version)==expected then set(new) as one caller-controlled atomic action.

slice.mechanism_summary: Connector-internal current-ETag acquisition protects the specialized label mutation against concurrent stale writes, while a caller-visible CAS requires an expected state/version to cross the read/write boundary. That binding is absent from the exposed schema.
slice.transfer_hypothesis: A caller-controlled CAS cell could serve scheduled-Chat durable coordination and duplicate/conflict defense without hosted compute; this Calendar surface cannot establish that property from schema alone.
slice.exact_component_benefit: Preserves the narrower conclusion that silent private-label assignment has provider-side lost-update protection, while preventing overclassification as a deterministic finite-state CAS primitive.
slice.measurable_effect: CAS-expressibility checklist: readable state identity=partial; caller-supplied expected version/state=absent; atomic compare predicate=absent; guarded write=present internally; generic idempotency token=absent. Result: 2 required CAS controls absent, so Phase-1 generic conditional-write acceptance is false.
slice.complexity_resource_estimate: Two connector-schema discovery calls; zero user semantic reads/writes; zero hosted compute; no provider operation executed; no paid/trial/monthly quota consumed by this audit leaf.
failure_edge_cases: A future connector schema could expose event ETag or expected-label preconditions; this result is scoped to the current exposed contract.
The set_event_label_silently result may contain useful state, but without a caller-supplied precondition it still cannot make a prior read and later write atomic.
An existing Google account, primary-calendar event, and pre-existing named label are prerequisites, so this is provider-specific and not provider-independent persistence.
Label cardinality/payload capacity is not established and may be insufficient for checkpoints even for blind assignment.
Zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental monetary cost are not established for actual Calendar use by schema-only inspection.
slice.contamination_independence: Used only current instruction controls, own cross_field LATEST/checkpoint, and current Google_Calendar connector schemas. No O/O-derived state, other worker state, downstream Comparator/Integrator, legacy pipeline semantics, shared substantive ledger, or user semantic data was consumed.
slice.reproducibility_notes: Re-run schema discovery for Google_Calendar labels/events and verify set_event_label_silently input remains exactly event_id+label_id with an internal current-ETag guard, while no read action yields a caller token accepted as a write precondition.
slice.keep_discard_reason: KEEP only as a provider-specific specialized guarded-assignment candidate; DISCARD as a caller-controlled deterministic CAS or Phase-1 parity acceptance mechanism.
